filessnap · Nov 21, 2026

What interests me here is the choice of the MIT license, not just the code release. It lets software vendors reuse the calculator directly, so the official rules can be embedded rather than reimplemented.

For a tax reform with new consumption taxes, I'd expect the real value to be a single reference implementation that everyone can test against, so different vendors don't each interpret the rules differently.

Does anyone know whether the repo accepts outside pull requests, or whether it's mainly published for transparency?

usr1106 · Nov 21, 2026

Embedding it correctly into closed source has the advantage it works correctly.

But no external can verify it really was done correctly, only a non-permissive license would allow that.
